record.title: Postmortem of database outage of January 31
record.summary: On January 31 2017, an engineer accidentally wiped the PostgreSQL data directory on GitLab.com's primary database server while trying to rebuild a lagging replication secondary, removing roughly 300GB of production data. This followed a spike in database load (from spam and a mistaken employee-deletion job) that broke replication, and recovery was severely hampered because pg_dump backups had been silently failing for months and Azure disk snapshots were not enabled for the database servers. GitLab.com was down for about 18 hours and was eventually restored from a 6-hour-old LVM snapshot, resulting in permanent loss of data (projects, comments, issues, user accounts) created between 17:20 and 00:00 UTC.

trigger.quote: Trying to restore the replication process, an engineer proceeds to wipe the PostgreSQL database directory, errantly thinking they were doing so on the secondary. Unfortunately this process was executed on the primary instead.
trigger.description: While trying to rebuild the lagging replication secondary, an engineer intended to wipe the secondary's PostgreSQL data directory but instead ran the wipe command against the primary database.

record.title: Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
record.summary: A latent race condition between two independent DynamoDB DNS Enactor processes caused an older DNS plan to overwrite a newer one for the DynamoDB regional endpoint in us-east-1, after which the plan cleanup process deleted the active plan and removed all IP addresses for the endpoint, leaving DNS automation in an inconsistent state that required manual intervention. This caused widespread DynamoDB API errors and connection failures beginning 11:48 PM PDT on October 19, which cascaded into EC2 instance launch failures (DWFM lease and Network Manager propagation issues), Network Load Balancer connection errors from health-check failover, and impact to numerous dependent AWS services (Lambda, ECS/EKS/Fargate, Connect, STS, IAM console sign-in, Redshift, Support Console, and others). Recovery occurred in stages between roughly 12:38 AM and 2:20 PM PDT on October 20, with some Redshift cluster recovery and Connect data backfill continuing afterward.

mechanism.label: race_condition
mechanism.quote: The root cause of this issue was a latent race condition in the DynamoDB DNS management system that resulted in an incorrect empty DNS record for the service's regional endpoint
mechanism.description: A race condition between two independently operating DNS Enactor processes caused a much older DNS plan to overwrite a newer one for the DynamoDB regional endpoint, and the plan cleanup process then deleted that plan, removing all IP addresses for the endpoint and leaving DNS automation unable to apply further updates.

mitigations.text: Temporary mitigations applied that enabled some internal services to connect to DynamoDB and repaired key internal tooling to unblock recovery.
Engineers throttled incoming work and began selective restarts of DWFM hosts to clear queues and re-establish droplet leases.
Engineers disabled automatic health check failovers for NLB, allowing healthy nodes and targets to be returned to service.
Re-enabled automatic DNS health check failover for NLB after EC2 recovered.
Throttled Lambda Event Source Mappings and asynchronous invocations to prioritize latency-sensitive synchronous invocations.
Restored the internal subsystem responsible for polling SQS queues and processed the message backlog.
Engineers took action to stop the Redshift replacement-workflow backlog from growing.
Engineers began relaxing EC2 request throttles as load stabilized.

record.title: 2023-03-08 Incident: Infrastructure connectivity issue affecting multiple regions | Datadog
record.summary: On March 8, 2023 at 06:00 UTC, a security update to systemd was automatically applied to VMs across five Datadog regions due to a legacy OS security update channel left enabled. This caused systemd-networkd to restart and forcibly delete the CNI-managed routes used by Cilium for container networking, knocking tens of thousands of nodes offline simultaneously across US1, EU1, US3, US4 and US5. The outage took down all Datadog services (browser/API access, ingestion, monitors) starting at 06:03 UTC. Recovery was staged over multiple days, with all services declared operational by March 9 and full resolution, including historical data backfill, on March 10.

Because the update's default trigger window (06:00-07:00 UTC) coincided across regions despite them running on different cloud providers with no direct network coupling, the outage hit all regions simultaneously, causing a platform-wide outage affecting access, data ingestion, and monitors. Datadog restored web access by 09:13 UTC, declared its first major service operational by 16:44 UTC on March 8, all services operational across regions by 08:58 UTC on March 9, and fully resolved the incident (including historical data backfill) by 06:25 UTC on March 10.

record.detection_quote: We were first alerted to the issue by our internal monitoring, three minutes after the trigger of the first faulty upgrade (March 8, 2023, at 06:00 UTC).

contributing_factors.text: A legacy security update channel was enabled in the base OS image used to run Kubernetes, causing the update to apply automatically rather than through normal change management.

The OS default automatic-update window (06:00-07:00 UTC) is the same across regions, causing multiple independent regions to be affected simultaneously despite having no direct network connection or coupling.
A fresh or rebooted node does not exhibit the issue since systemd-networkd normally starts before CNI routing rules are installed, so no obvious test reproduced the exact failure sequence.

Different cloud providers' auto-scaling logic behaved differently: some replaced unhealthy nodes immediately causing data loss and a thundering herd against regional rate limits, complicating recovery.

Quorum-based control-plane data stores degrade to a full outage once quorum is lost, unlike share-nothing statically sharded stores which degrade more gracefully, complicating recovery of metadata systems.

record.title: October 21 post-incident analysis
record.summary: A brief network partition caused by routine maintenance on optical equipment triggered Orchestrator to fail over GitHub's MySQL primaries from the US East Coast to the US West Coast data center. Because both data centers ended up with un-replicated writes, GitHub could not safely fail back, and chose to prioritize data integrity over availability, resulting in 24 hours and 11 minutes of degraded service including paused webhooks and GitHub Pages builds. Recovery required restoring multiple terabytes of MySQL backups, resyncing replicas, and processing a large backlog of queued webhook and Pages jobs before service was declared fully restored.

record.title: External Technical Root Cause Analysis — Channel File 291
record.summary: In February 2024, CrowdStrike introduced a new IPC Template Type whose definition expected 21 input fields, but the sensor integration code only supplied 20, a mismatch that evaded testing and validation. On July 19, 2024, new Rapid Response Content in Channel File 291 introduced a non-wildcard matching criterion on the 21st field, which combined with a missing bounds check in the Content Interpreter to cause an out-of-bounds memory read and system crash (BSOD) on Windows sensors that received the update. record.summary: On June 12, 2025, a policy change containing unintended blank fields was inserted into the regional Spanner tables used by Google's Service Control system, replicating globally within seconds. This exercised a code path in a Service Control feature (added May 29, 2025) that lacked error handling and feature-flag protection, causing a null pointer crash that put Service Control binaries into a global crash loop. This resulted in a spike of 503 errors across many Google Cloud, Workspace, and Security Operations products. Recovery was achieved within about 40 minutes for most regions via a 'red-button' rollback, but us-central1 suffered a herd-effect overload of its Spanner backend that took up to ~2h40m to fully resolve.

record.title: Slack’s Incident on 2-22-22
record.summary: On February 22, 2022, a routine percentage-based Consul agent upgrade caused memcached nodes to be repeatedly deregistered and re-registered, and the new Mcrib control-plane component quickly refilled the cache ring with empty nodes, driving down cache hit rates. Because a channel-membership query used during client boot fell back to an expensive 'scatter query' across every shard of a user-sharded Vitess keyspace when data was missing from cache, rising cache misses overwhelmed the database and triggered a cascading failure. Client boot requests failed widely, and Slack responded by throttling boot requests, pausing the Consul rollout, and modifying the query to fetch only missing data and read from replicas, eventually restoring service.

This triggered a cascading failure in which an inefficient 'scatter query' for Group Direct Message membership, normally masked by caching, overwhelmed the Vitess database as cache misses rose, causing client boot failures and Slack outages for many users. Responders mitigated the incident by throttling client boot requests and later fixed the query to reduce load, restoring normal service.

trigger.label: infrastructure_maintenance
trigger.quote: The PBR step on February 22 updated Consul on 25% of the fleet. It followed two previous 25% steps the prior week, both of which had occurred without any incident.
trigger.description: A percentage-based rollout (PBR) step upgrading the Consul agent on 25% of the fleet caused memcached nodes to sequentially deregister and be replaced with empty cache nodes by Mcrib, right before peak traffic.

change_at.quote: The PBR step on February 22 updated Consul on 25% of the fleet.

mechanism.label: cascading_overload
mechanism.quote: we hit a tipping point and entered a cascading failure scenario as we hit peak traffic for the day
mechanism.description: Cache churn from Consul agent restarts combined with an inefficient scatter query caused cache hit rates to collapse, overwhelming the Vitess database with scatter queries and creating a self-sustaining cascading failure that prevented client boot requests from succeeding.

detected_at.quote: Just after 6 a.m. Pacific Time, a number of things happened almost simultaneously: we began to receive user tickets about problems connecting to Slack, some internal users experienced problems using Slack, and a number of our engineering teams received pages or alerts about problems.

mitigations.text: Throttled client boot requests to reduce database load.
Paused the Consul agent restart operation that had triggered the problem.
Modified the inefficient scatter query to read only missing data from Vitess rather than querying every shard, and to read from replicas as well as primaries.
Slowly increased the client boot rate limit back to normal levels while maximizing database goodput until service was fully restored.

record.title: Roblox Return to Service  | Roblox
record.summary: Roblox suffered a 73-hour outage from October 28-31, 2021, after enabling a Consul streaming feature on a traffic-routing service under very high read/write load caused severe Go channel contention, which combined with a pathological BoltDB freelist performance bug to make the single shared Consul cluster unresponsive. Because Nomad, Vault, and most internal services depended on Consul for service discovery, this cascaded into a near-total platform outage, and the diagnosis was slowed because telemetry systems themselves depended on the unhealthy Consul cluster. Roblox and HashiCorp engineers went through several rounds of hardware replacement, cluster resets, and load reduction before identifying and disabling the streaming feature, then worked around a related 'slow leader' issue and rebuilt the caching layer before gradually reopening access to players.

trigger.label: config_change
trigger.quote: On October 27th at 14:00, one day before the outage, we enabled this feature on a backend service that is responsible for traffic routing.
trigger.description: Roblox enabled the Consul streaming feature (with concurrent 50% node increase) on a backend traffic-routing service on October 27th at 14:00, one day before the outage began.

change_at.quote: On October 27th at 14:00, one day before the outage, we enabled this feature on a backend service that is responsible for traffic routing.

mechanism.label: lock_contention
mechanism.quote: Under very high load – specifically, both a very high read load and a very high write load – the design of streaming exacerbates the amount of contention on a single Go channel, which causes blocking during writes, making it significantly less efficient.
mechanism.description: Under very high concurrent read and write load, the Consul streaming feature's reduced use of Go channel concurrency controls caused severe contention that, combined with a pathological BoltDB freelist performance issue, drove Consul KV write latency from ~300ms to ~2s, making the single shared Consul cluster unhealthy and cascading failures into all dependent Roblox services.

mitigations.text: Replaced Consul cluster nodes with new, more powerful 128-core machines with faster NVMe disks.

Configured iptables to block internal traffic to Consul during the controlled restart.
Disabled all non-essential Consul usage, scaled down service instance counts, and decreased health check frequency.
Reverted Consul cluster hardware from 128-core back to 64-core servers.
Disabled the Consul streaming feature across all systems, which lowered KV write latency back to normal.
Worked around the slow-leader problem by preventing problematic leaders from staying elected.
Redeployed and repaired the caching system to restore a healthy state.
Used DNS steering to gradually ramp up player access in ~10% increments while monitoring stability.

resolved_at.quote: At 16:45 Sunday, 73 hours after the start of the outage, 100% of players were given access and Roblox was fully operational.
